newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slump as foreign sentiment sours.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slump as foreign sentiment sours.

text.p: Mexican stocks slumped, breaking support in early trade Wednesday as foreign sentiment on Mexico was soured by some reversals in the country's privatization effort, analysts said.
"Dealers almost completely ignored earnings reports, they're very nervous as we can see from the weak peso and foreigners bailing out of the market," said a Mexico City analyst.
The blue chip IPC index .MXX was down 31.36 points, or 0.98 percent, at 3,167.72. The benchmark 48-hour peso meanwhile tumbled eight centavos to 7.99/8.02 per dollar.

Analysts noted that foreign investors were concerned by the Mexican government's backtracking on petrochemical privatization plans, and were further dismayed by a bill to postpone setting up privatized pension funds (Afores) that was sent to Congress on Monday.
They also noted that investors were nervous ahead of official economic policy criteria due out in a few weeks. The criteria include guidelines for monetary policy for the upcoming year.
On the broad market, just one stock, steelmaker Hylsamex, was ahead, while 64 were down out of 73 stocks traded.
